content.text:
I didn't change any code this time. Every drag-to-reorder in the app already shows the macOS-style insertion line from the shared rule in the spec (`DragReorderBehaviour`), which was added earlier in this session.

There are only two places where you can drag to reorder, and both use it:
- **Queued prompts:** a horizontal line appears in the gap where the prompt will land.
- **File tabs:** a vertical line appears in the gap between tabs.

In both, the line is a 2px accent line with a small open circle at its leading end, drawn on top so nothing shifts during the drag. Which gap it marks depends on which half of an item the pointer is over. No line appears where a drop would change nothing, and the dragged item stays in place at half opacity. The other drags in the app resize panels or drop files into the chat input, so they don't reorder anything and get no line.

The four drag tests pass. That includes one that pauses mid-drag and checks the line is drawn and no row is highlighted.

**One problem is still open, and it's in the spec, not the code:** the spec says the gap between Chat and the first file tab never shows the line. That keeps Chat first, but it also means you can never drag a file tab into the first file position. The code follows the spec as written. This step was code-only, so I couldn't change the spec. The fix is to let that gap accept file tabs, since Chat can't be dragged anyway. Ask for it as a spec change and I'll update both.

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1790755082-Prompt_3a0124c1879b9e0a.understanding.md`.
